newsitem.title: FRANCE: COOPERATION NEEDED TO AVOID CAPACITY LOGJAMS - IATA.
newsitem.headline: COOPERATION NEEDED TO AVOID CAPACITY LOGJAMS - IATA.

text.p: All sectors of the aviation industry must work together to avoid future growth being stifled by lack of capacity, International Airline Transport Association (IATA) director general Pierre Jeanniot said.

This is essential:"to avoid the system bottlenecks which could choke off tomorrow's growth as well as frustrating passengers and shippers," he told the annual meeting of Airports Council International (ACI) on Monday.
An extra margin in the infrastructure capacity is essential to cope with expected annual air transport growth over the next 15 to 20 years of six to seven percent annually.
"Airlines often feel they are the only ones....who have to change and adapt " and apart from system capacity there are three other areas which are fundamental to the air transport industry's future.
These are the need for airports to charge reasonable unit costs, the tackling of environmental questions and ensuring customer service.

"Airlines do not take kindly to passengers'perceptions of good airline service being completely eroded by negative perceptions of security checks, immigration, health checks and customs, by putting much-needed commercial outlets in the wrong place and by crowding in departure and arrival areas."

Airlines find "a rapidly increasing share of airline costs arises from monopoly suppliers....and that frequent examples of this are provided by airports and en-route navigation facilities," Jeanniot said.
During 1991-95 user charges levied by airports on IATA airline rose 48 percent while en-route navigation service charges jumped 75 percent, he added.
In 1995 airlines paid $6.2 billion in airport landing and parking charges, and $4.9 billion for navigation services, 9.3 percent of total operating costs, he said.
Other costs including ticketing and sales 18.2 percent, crew and passenger services 13.7 percent, insurance and depreciation 12.5 percent with fuel and oil at 10.9 percent, Jeanniot noted.

"Good airports" included "BAA Plc, probably the most profitable in the world... and where charges have decreased over the years," and Ireland's Aer Rianta where charges are today practically at 1987 levels as well as the Singapore Airport Authority where charges have only increased by five percent since it was commercialised 14 years ago. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
